dispositions.status: resolved in planning contract at reviewedHeadSha
evidence: Restore/import creates a fresh workspace execution epoch, fences source leases/attempts and persists restoreHold before supervisor requeue/recovery.
Copied queued/in-flight jobs, proposals and approvals cannot authorize effects; terminal receipts remain historical evidence.
Provider account/request identities and uncertain reservations are retained; copied state cannot resubmit or assume release/refund while the original workspace may remain active.

Explicit authorized reconciliation/restart is required, including local renders; repeat restore/open/restart must cause zero spawns, submissions, attachment publications or automatic reservation releases.
The contract and fault cases are propagated into docs14/17/20 and rendered/machine task specifications YU-013/014/061/080.
dispositions.repairAssessment: The repair closes the missing restore authority boundary and explicitly overrides the existing stale-attempt requeue behavior for copied state. It preserves uncertainty instead of treating a historical backup as proof of external outcome.

dispositions.status: addressed in planning contract at reviewedHeadSha
dispositions.section: Document transport without widening command limits
evidence: A separate authenticated project-scoped streamed staging route bounds both raw and canonical whole-document UTF-8 bytes to 8 MiB; general 2 MiB command/snapshot limits remain unchanged.
Staging receipts bind project/principal/hash/kind/request digest and expiry; private handles never expose server host paths.
Admission reserves bytes before upload; proposed concurrency/aggregate/TTL limits, nested complexity validation and rejection of embedded pixels/URLs are explicit.
Commit reopens/rehashes outside the DB write transaction, excludes cleanup, atomically consumes the handle with the revision and returns receipt replay after expiry/cleanup.
YU-010 requires real transport, UTF-8/escape expansion, disconnect, foreign/expired/changed handle and cleanup/commit race cases.
dispositions.repairAssessment: This is a coherent bounded transport decision rather than an implicit global ingress increase. Proposed ceilings remain qualification candidates.

dispositions.status: addressed in planning contract at reviewedHeadSha
evidence: Every denial is paired with same-receipt/environment unrestricted sentinel access, live restricted-worker execution and authorized staging IO controls.
Permitted descendants must execute only in the named profile; missing/crashed workers and unreachable sentinels invalidate a denial result.
YU-041 machine/rendered tests and negative tests carry those requirements.
dispositions.repairAssessment: The evidence contract now rejects vacuous isolation passes while preserving separate GPU/runtime qualification.

additionalConsistency.section: Shared activation gate and legacy saves
additionalConsistency.assessment: AG-DOCS prevents isolated schema/migration tasks from promoting live v5 persistence before YU-010 through YU-015 complete recovery and legacy-save evidence. Existing/full-save paths must preserve creative/nested references or explicitly refuse; this supports the repaired authority and closure contracts.

residualConcerns.detail: No restoreHold, upload staging, resource-boundary, race, Windows isolation or positive-control fixture was executed by this delta review. Future implementation still needs the declared deterministic/native/browser tests and independent review.

Actual account-scoped reconciliation, shared budget authority across original/restored copies, provider idempotency and unknown-submit handling remain adapter-specific qualification work. The repaired plan safely holds copied execution state; it does not prove that a provider can guarantee stop, refund or duplicate-charge avoidance. Keep those routes disabled until their separate gates pass.
